# Adjudication Task — Chapter 286

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃286화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그날 새벽, 헌터들이 자주 이용하는 인기 포럼 사이트에 짤막한 게시글이 올라왔다.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|형들 나 이상한 꿈 꿨는데 해몽 좀;
 10|
 11|
 12|
 13|정확한 건 밝힐 수 없는데 나름 방귀 좀 뀌는 대형 길드 보안팀 소속임. 암튼 이게 중요한 건 아니고.
 14|
 15|평소처럼 근무하던 중에 깜빡 졸았거든? 근데 꿈에 시벌좌가 나온 거야.
 16|
 17|이상한 놈이 자꾸 얼쩡거린다길래 사수(매국노 새끼임. 내 생각에 얘 본명 야마모토 같은데 숨기고 있음.)랑 같이 잡으러 갔는데, 그게 바로 시벌좌였던 거.
 18|
 19|그런데 딱 여기까지만 또렷하게 기억나. 그 후에는 사수가 유도리 하고, 내가 이랏샤이마세 하는 걸로 끝남.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|(Best 댓글) 해몽 전에 이 글 해석해 줄 사람 있냐. 이 새1끼 도대체 뭔 소리 하는 건지 모르겠네.
 24|
 25|└ 222
 26|
 27|└ 다른 건 그렇다 치고 유도리하고 이랏샤이마세는 뭐냐; 맥락을 파악할 수가 없다.
 28|
 29|└ 사수는 왜 매국노임? 유키늘로에서 히트텍 삼?
 30|
 31|└ (작성자) 킹시국에 자꾸 일본어 쓰니까 그렇지. 평소에도 유도리, 겐세이. 뭐 그런 단어 많이 씀.
 32|
 33|└ 넌 이랏샤이마세 했다며.
 34|
 35|└ (작성자) 응.
 36|
 37|└ 미친놈이네. 응 ㅇㅈㄹㅋㅋㅋ
 38|
 39|└ 고문관 냄새 진동한다. 사수 개불쌍.
 40|
 41|└ (작성자) 근데 사수한테 이 꿈 내용 말했더니 자기도 비슷한 꿈 꿨다더라고. 시벌좌가 우리 길드원들 백 명 뚜까패고 아레스 부길마랑 맞짱 떴대.
 42|
 43|└ 작성자 새끼 뚜까패고 싶네.
 44|
 45|└ (작성자) 진짜라니까;;; 그러더니 자기 폰 없어졌다고 나한테 지랄함;; 최신형 어른폰이라 없어져서 빡친 듯.
 46|
 47|
 48|
 49|안녕하세요. 현직 무당입니다. 글에서 심상치 않은 기운이 느껴져서 그러는데, 더 자세히 말씀해 주실 수 있나요?
 50|
 51|└ (작성자) 헉, 정말 무당이신가요?
 52|
 53|└ 아뇨. 구란데요.
 54|
 55|└ (작성자) 헉. 미친 새끼신가요?
 56|
 57|
 58|
 59|게시글은 불과 10분도 되지 않아 삭제되었다.
 60|
 61|해당 글을 본 사람들은 관심 병자 하나가 사라진 것에 크게 신경 쓰지 않았고, 이러한 일련의 과정에서 아레스 길드가 개입했음을 의심하는 사람 또한 없었다.
 62|
 63|아, 물론 나는 제외다.
 64|
 65|‘정신계 마법으로 기억을 조작했겠지.’
 66|
 67|명백한 범법 행위지만, 블랙 헌터도 양성하는 놈들이 그걸 따지는 게 더 우습다.
 68|
 69|댓글 내용 중에 어른폰이 사라졌다는 얘기가 있는 걸 보면 꼼꼼하게 핸드폰까지 일일이 확인한 모양이었다.
 70|
 71|‘결정적인 증거였는데.’
 72|
 73|내 전용 카메라맨은 박태섭과 박지훈이 등장하기 무섭게 밖으로 튀었고, 그대로 아레스 길드의 수중에 떨어졌다.
 74|
 75|뭐, 그리 아쉽지는 않았다. 어차피 빌딩을 나오면서 몸수색을 받았기 때문이다. 놈들은 내 공유 클라우드 폴더까지 확인한 후 돌려주었다.
 76|
 77|거기에 한 마디 경고를 덧붙이는 섬세함도 잊지 않았다.
 78|
 79|
 80|
 81|‘혹시나 숨기고 있는 게 있으면 지금이라도 삭제하십시오. 감추고 있다가 걸리면 재미없을 겁니다.’
 82|
 83|
 84|
 85|안 그래도 핸드폰에 넣어 둔 야동이 걸리는 바람에 마음이 영 언짢았는데, 말하는 놈의 말투가 보통 띠꺼운 수준이 아니었다.
 86|
 87|지금 같은 상황만 아니었어도 한 방 먹여 줬을 것이다.
 88|
 89|‘면상 똑똑히 기억해 뒀다. 이 깍두기같이 생긴 새끼야.’
 90|
 91|각진 얼굴에 스포츠머리를 한 놈이었다. 일의 뒤처리를 맡은 데다 다른 놈들이 팀장님, 팀장님 하는 것을 보니 이정룡의 오른팔쯤 되는 놈인 모양이다.
 92|
 93|[기감]으로 확인한 이름은 석고준. 사실 이름까지 알아낸 이유에는 놈의 실력도 한몫했다.
 94|
 95|‘그 자식도 무공 비스무리한 걸 익힌 것 같던데.’
 96|
 97|한 번 눈에 의심이 깃들자, 전보다 더 명확하게 볼 수 있었다.
 98|
 99|이정룡이 남기고 간 아레스 길드원들은 하나같이 보통 놈들이 아니었다. 혼자서도 평범한 A급 헌터 두 명은 찜 쪄 먹는 실력자들.
100|
101|그중에서도 석고준에게서 받은 느낌은…… 솔직히 말해서 내심 놀랄 정도였다.
102|
103|놈의 띠꺼운 말투는 실력에서 나오는 자신감이었다.
104|
105|‘어떻게 이런 놈들을 길러 냈지?’
106|
107|혹시 진짜 무공? 아니면 아레스 길드 내부에서 독자적으로 개발해 낸 무술일 수도 있다. 여러 가지 의문들이 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 늘어진다.
108|
109|내가 곰곰이 생각에 잠겨 있던 그때였다.
110|
111|“이 선생님. 임혁준 환자 의식 돌아왔습니다!”
112|
113|문밖, 복도에서 들려온 간호사의 외침에 벌떡 일어났다.
114|
115|임혁준. 거의 불리지 않는 임꺽정의 본명이다. 그가 장장 사흘 만에 의식을 회복한 것이다.
116|
117|
118|
119|* * *
120|
121|
122|
123|“여보! 준이 아빠!”
124|
125|“아빠아!”
126|
127|당장이라도 병실 문을 열어젖히고 싶은 마음을 꾹 눌러 참았다. 지금은 가족들의 시간이다.
128|
129|사흘 동안 의식을 잃고 있었던 남편, 아버지를 만난 아내와 아이들의 울음소리가 병실 문틈 사이로 흘러나왔다.
130|
131|그렇게 한바탕 통곡의 파도가 휩쓸고 한참 후에야 우리 차례가 왔다.
132|
133|“어, 다들 왔어?”
134|
135|젠장. 첫마디부터 목이 꽉 막힌다.
136|
137|임꺽정은 환한 웃음과 함께 두 팔을 벌리다가 코를 찡그렸다.
138|
139|“윽.”
140|
141|“팔, 팔 조심하세요. 팔!”
142|
143|“괜찮을 줄 알았는데, 움직일 때 조금 쑤시네.”
144|
145|“떨어진 팔을 도로 붙였는데 바로 괜찮아지면 그게 사람이에요? 변신 로봇이지.”
146|
147|송송이가 핀잔을 주며 치료 주문을 외웠다. 통증이 훨씬 가라앉았는지 임꺽정의 안색이 한결 편안해진다.
148|
149|“고마워, 송 양.”
150|
151|“고마우면 제발 조심하세요. 치료사 말 못 들었어요? 최소 2주 정도는 무리하지 말고 쉬어야 한다고요.”
152|
153|“그런 말도 고맙고.”
154|
155|“아저씨!”
156|
157|“아이고, 귀청 떨어지겠네.”
158|
159|산적처럼 껄껄 웃는 저 모습이 이렇게도 반가울 줄이야.
160|
161|전처럼 호탕한 웃음을 터트린 임꺽정이 다른 사람들에게 고개를 돌렸다.
162|
163|“김 형, 아니 길드장님. 정말 고맙습니다. 저 쓰러져 있는 동안 많이 신경 써 주셨다고 애들 엄마한테 들었어요.”
164|
165|김 집사가 작게 고개를 저었다.
166|
167|“고마워하실 필요도 없는 당연한 일이었습니다. 같은 길드 식구가 이런 일을 당했는데 발 벗고 나서야죠.”
168|
169|“듣자 하니 비용도 많이 쓰셨다고…….”
170|
171|임꺽정의 치료에는 유명한 힐러가 초빙되었고 한 병에 억대는 우습게 호가하는 상급 포션이 아낌없이 쏟아 부어졌다.
172|
173|예전에도 그랬다지만, 사람 목숨도 값을 매기는 세상이다. 내세울 것이라고는 경력밖에 없는 D급 헌터에게 누가 이렇게 해 주겠는가.
174|
175|축축하게 젖은 임꺽정의 목소리에 김 집사가 낮게 웃었다.
176|
177|“굳이 감사 인사를 하셔야겠다면 전주(錢主)에게 하시죠. 얼굴마담인 저는 빠지겠습니다.”
178|
179|그 말에 임꺽정의 시선이 전주를 향해 스르륵 움직였다.
180|
181|“최 팀장.”
182|
183|열양지기라도 담겼는지 목소리가 후끈후끈하다. 최 팀장은 그가 뭐라고 말을 잇기도 전에 먼저 선수를 쳐 버렸다.
184|
185|“임꺽정 씨의 잘못이 아니라, 우리 길드가 얕보여서 당한 겁니다. 이런 불상사를 막지 못한 제 잘못이고 불찰이니 오히려 죄송해야 할 사람은 바로 접니다.”
186|
187|“최 팀자아앙!”
188|
189|단지 옆에 서 있는 것만으로도 흉악범을 모범수로 둔갑시키는 임꺽정의 눈동자에 눈물이 그렁그렁하다.
190|
191|그가 팔을 뻗어 껴안으려 하자 최 팀장이 흠칫 놀라며 물러났다.
192|
193|“파, 팔 조심하셔야죠.”
194|
195|“이 정도는 괜찮아. 한 번만 안아 보고 싶어서 그래.”
196|
197|“……그런 영광스러운 기회는 마지막 한 사람한테 넘기고 싶네요.”
198|
199|그다지 영광스러운 기회는 아닌 것 같지만, 어쨌든 결국 내 차례가 돌아왔다.
200|
201|“…….”
202|
203|“…….”
204|
205|순간 침묵이 내려앉았다.
206|
207|임꺽정이 깨어난다면 꼭 해 주고 싶은 말이 있었는데, 막상 깨어난 그를 마주하자 조개처럼 입이 꾹 다물어진다.
208|
209|먼저 침묵을 깨트린 것은 임꺽정이었다.
210|
211|“어때?”
212|
213|“네?”
214|
215|“우리 와이프랑 애들. 예쁘지?”
216|
217|밑도 끝도 없이 튀어나온 가족 자랑에 나도 모르게 실소를 머금었다.
218|
219|“네. 그러네요.”
220|
221|“너희 형수가 좀 미인이어야지.”
222|
223|“인정합니다. 혹시 감금이나 협박했어요?”
224|
225|“열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다. 명심해. 나는 마흔일곱 번째에 성공했어.”
226|
227|“방금은 열 번 찍어서 안 넘어가는 나무 없다면서요.”
228|
229|임꺽정이 킬킬거리며 웃었다.
230|
231|“있긴 있더라고. 열 번으로는 택도 없는 나무가.”
232|
233|“불구속 입건 되지 않은 게 용하네요.”
234|
235|“자식아, 그때 포기했으면 저런 미인을 얻었겠냐?”
236|
237|얼굴이 퉁퉁 부은 임꺽정의 아내가 얼굴을 가리며 손사래 친다.
238|
239|아직 초등학생인 아이 둘은 언제 울었냐는 듯 똘망똘망한 눈빛으로 나를 신기하게 쳐다봤다.
240|
241|“아빠. 누구예요?”
242|
243|“누구야? 누구야!”
244|
245|임꺽정이 엉겨 붙는 아이들을 끌어안으며 대답했다.
246|
247|“삼촌이야. 태경이 삼촌.”
248|
249|“태경이 삼촌?”
250|
251|“응, 아빠가 말한 적 있었지? 잘생기고 힘센 삼촌 있다고.”
252|
253|가족들에게 내 이야기를 했었구나.
254|
255|가슴 한구석으로부터 따뜻한 온기가 번져 나간다. 나를 바라보는 아이들의 눈망울이 한층 더 빛났다.
256|
257|원래 어린애들이야 예쁘고 귀엽다지만 이 자매는 아역 배우를 해도 되겠다. 이게 바로 모계 유전자의 승리구나.
258|
259|“와아! 아저씨가 태경이 삼촌이에요?”
260|
261|“만나서 방갑슴미다!”
262|
263|절로 흐뭇한 웃음이 지어진다.
264|
265|나는 두 아이의 머리를 쓰다듬으며 임꺽정에게 말했다.
266|
267|“애들이 귀엽네요. 천진난만하고.”
268|
269|“그걸 말이라고. 너도 결혼하고 딸 낳아 봐라. 왜 딸바보, 딸바보 하는지 알게 될 테니까.”
270|
271|나도 고등학생 때 별명이 딸바보였다. 물론 딸은 없었지만.
272|
273|어쨌건 이 화목한 네 가족을 보고 있자니 마음이 뭉클해진다.
274|
275|임꺽정이 아직 뻣뻣한 움직임으로 팔을 들어 나를 껴안았다. 예전과는 비교도 안 되게 약해진 힘이 실린 손바닥이 내 등을 두드린다.
276|
277|툭. 툭.
278|
279|“고맙다. 항상 고마워.”
280|
281|그 말을 듣는 순간, 나는 줄곧 마음속에 품고 있던 한 가지 결심을 굳혔다.
282|
283|‘같은 실수를 반복해서는 안 돼.’
284|
285|마음속으로 뇌까리며 힘주어 임꺽정을 안았다.
286|
287|오늘은 한 남자가 가족과 친구들의 곁으로 돌아온 날이었다.
288|
289|
290|
291|* * *
292|
293|
294|
295|한 시간 후, 병실에는 나와 임꺽정을 포함한 평화 길드원 다섯 사람만이 남아 있었다.
296|

“Ugh.”

[P49]
“Your arm! Be careful with your arm!”

[P50]
“I thought it would be fine, but it aches a little when I move it.”

[P51]
“They reattached a severed arm. Did you think it would be fine right away? What are you, a transforming robot?”

[P52]
Song Song scolded him while casting a healing spell. Once the pain subsided, Im Kkeokjeong’s expression relaxed considerably.

[P53]
“Thank you, Miss Song.”

[P54]
“If you’re grateful, please be careful. Didn’t you hear the healer? You need to rest and avoid overexerting yourself for at least two weeks.”

[P55]
“And thank you for saying that, too.”

[P56]
“Uncle!”

[P57]
“Ow, there go my eardrums.”

[P58]
I never would have imagined how happy it could make me to see him laughing heartily like a bandit.

[P59]
After letting out the same boisterous laugh as before, Im Kkeokjeong turned to the others.

[P60]
“Hyung Kim—no, Guild Master. Thank you so much. The kids’ mother told me how well you looked after me while I was unconscious.”

[P61]
Butler Kim shook his head slightly.

[P62]
“There’s no need to thank me. It was only natural. When one of our Guild members suffers something like this, of course we step up.”

[P63]
“I heard you spent quite a lot of money, too…”

[P64]
A renowned healer had been brought in to treat Im Kkeokjeong, and high-grade potions that cost well over a hundred million won per bottle had been used without restraint.

[P65]
It might have been the same in the past, but this was a world where even a human life had a price. Who would go this far for a D-rank Hunter with nothing to his name but years of experience?

[P66]
Butler Kim chuckled softly at the emotion thickening Im Kkeokjeong’s voice.

[P67]
“If you really must thank someone, thank the man footing the bill. I’m just the figurehead, so leave me out of it.”

[P68]
At those words, Im Kkeokjeong’s gaze slowly shifted toward the man footing the bill.

[P69]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P70]
His voice burned as though it carried Scorching Yang Qi. Before Im Kkeokjeong could continue, Team Leader Choi cut him off.

[P71]
“This wasn’t your fault, Mr. Im. It happened because our Guild was looked down on. I failed to prevent it, so if anyone owes an apology, it’s me.”

[P72]
“Team Leader Choi!”

[P73]
Standing next to Im Kkeokjeong was enough to make the worst thug look like a model prisoner, yet tears now brimmed in his eyes.

[P74]
When he reached out to embrace him, Team Leader Choi flinched and stepped back.

[P75]
“B-be careful with your arm.”

[P76]
“It’s fine. I just want to hug you once.”

[P77]
“…I’d like to pass that glorious opportunity on to the last person.”

[P78]
It didn’t seem like much of an honor, but in the end, my turn came.

[P79]
“…”

[P80]
“…”

[P81]
Silence fell.

[P82]
There was something I had desperately wanted to say to Im Kkeokjeong once he woke up, but now that I was standing face-to-face with him, my mouth clamped shut like a clam.

[P83]
Im Kkeokjeong broke the silence first.

[P84]
“What do you think?”

[P85]
“About what?”

[P86]
“My wife and kids. Pretty, right?”

[P87]
His out-of-nowhere bragging about his family drew a quiet laugh from me.

[P88]
“Yes. They are.”

[P89]
“Your sister-in-law is quite the beauty.”

[P90]
“I’ll give you that. Did you imprison or threaten her?”

[P91]
“There’s no tree that won’t fall after ten chops. Remember that. I succeeded on the forty-seventh.”

[P92]
“You just said every tree falls after ten chops.”

[P93]
Im Kkeokjeong snickered.

[P94]
“Turns out there are some that won’t. Ten chops didn’t even make a dent.”

[P95]
“It’s a miracle you weren’t charged.”

[P96]
“You idiot. If I’d given up back then, do you think I could have gotten a beauty like that?”

[P97]
Im Kkeokjeong’s wife, her face swollen from crying, covered it with one hand and waved the other dismissively.

[P98]
His two children, both still in elementary school, stared at me with bright, curious eyes as though they had never cried at all.

[P99]
“Daddy, who is he?”

[P100]
“Who is he? Who?”

[P101]
Im Kkeokjeong pulled the clinging children into his arms and answered.

[P102]
“He’s your uncle. Uncle Taekyung.”

[P103]
“Uncle Taekyung?”

[P104]
“Yeah. I’ve told you about him before, right? The handsome, strong uncle.”

[P105]
So he had told his family about me.

[P106]
Warmth spread from somewhere deep in my chest. The children’s eyes sparkled even more brightly as they looked at me.

[P107]
All children were cute, but these sisters could have been child actors. This was the triumph of maternal genes.

[P108]
“Wow! You’re Uncle Taekyung?”

[P109]
“Nice ta meet you!”

[P110]
A fond smile spread across my face.

[P111]
I patted both girls on the head and said to Im Kkeokjeong, “They’re adorable. So innocent.”

[P112]
“Obviously. Get married and have a daughter yourself. Then you’ll understand why people call men doting dads.”

[P113]
I’d been nicknamed a doting dad in high school, too. Of course, I hadn’t had a daughter.

[P114]
In any case, the sight of this close-knit family of four made my heart swell.

[P115]
Im Kkeokjeong raised his arm stiffly and embraced me. His hand, far weaker than before, patted my back.

[P116]
Tap. Tap.

[P117]
“Thank you. I’m always grateful.”

[P118]
The moment I heard those words, my resolve hardened around a decision I had been carrying all this time.

[P119]
*I can’t make the same mistake again.*

[P120]
I repeated the words to myself and hugged Im Kkeokjeong tightly.

[P121]
Today, one man had returned to his family and friends.

[P122]
* * *

[P123]
An hour later, only five members of the Peace Guild remained in the hospital room, including Im Kkeokjeong and me.

[P124]
Im Kkeokjeong’s wife wanted her husband to rest, but his resolve was firm.

[P125]
“I almost left my beloved wife and kids behind. I need to hear it now. Everything that happened, without leaving out a single detail.”

[P126]
There was a new firmness in the good-natured man who had always been softhearted and full of laughter.

[P127]
By the time he had heard the entire story, Im Kkeokjeong’s face was rigid.

[P128]
“It was Ares Guild?”

[P129]
“Yes.”

[P130]
“And the Lee Jungryong you mentioned really is that Lee Jungryong?”

[P131]
“I’m sure.”

[P132]
“…Hah.”

[P133]
A groanlike sigh escaped him.

[P134]
We had caught the tail of the Black Hunters and found the body called Myeongdong Guild. When we pressed down on that body, the head that emerged was Ares Guild.

[P135]
The problem was that this was no ordinary head.

[P136]
“We followed a snake’s tail and found a dragon’s head.”

[P137]
As I spoke, I glanced sidelong at Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim. Both wore the same calm expressions as always.

[P138]
But I had seen it clearly.

[P139]
Before Im Kkeokjeong regained consciousness, when I first mentioned Ares Guild, turbulent waves had surged through both men’s eyes.

[P140]
*There’s definitely something going on…*

[P141]
I didn’t know exactly what. Song Song and I had sensed something strange and questioned them relentlessly, but they had clammed up after briefly saying they would tell us once Im Kkeokjeong woke up.

[P142]
*But now it’s time for them to talk.*

[P143]
Perhaps he sensed our gazes. Team Leader Choi was just about to speak when—

[P144]
Thud. Thud.

[P145]
Countless noises mingled in the hospital hallway, but those footsteps were different. Unusually heavy, with a deep resonance.

[P146]
And they carried qi.

[P147]
“They’re coming.”

[P148]
At my words, everyone rose from their seats.

[P149]
Sure enough, the footsteps stopped outside our hospital room.

[P150]
Knock, knock.

[P151]
The door opened, revealing a face I had seen only half a day ago.

[P152]
*Go Jun?*

[P153]
Wait. If that bastard was here, then could it be…?

[P154]
The thought broke off. Go Jun’s face vanished from view as another man strode into the hospital room.

[P155]
He was nearing seventy, yet his youthful appearance made him look like a man in his forties. He possessed a leader’s charisma and a natural air of intimidation.

[P156]
*Lee Jungryong.*

[P157]
His gaze swept over us before stopping dead on one person. The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.

[P158]
“You’ve grown.”

[P159]
Team Leader Choi’s gaze sank as he looked at Lee Jungryong.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. “I heard you spent quite a lot of money, too…”

[P64]
A renowned healer had been brought in to treat Im Kkeokjeong, and high-grade potions that cost well over a hundred million won per bottle had been used without restraint.

[P65]
It might have been the same in the past, but this was a world where even a human life had a price. Who would go this far for a D-rank Hunter with nothing to his name but years of experience?

[P66]
Butler Kim chuckled softly at the emotion thickening Im Kkeokjeong’s voice.

[P67]
“If you really must thank someone, thank the man footing the bill. I’m just the figurehead, so leave me out of it.”

[P68]
At those words, Im Kkeokjeong’s gaze slowly shifted toward the man footing the bill.

[P69]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P70]
His voice burned as though it carried Scorching Yang Qi. Before Im Kkeokjeong could continue, Team Leader Choi cut him off.

[P71]
“This wasn’t your fault, Mr. Im. It happened because our Guild was looked down on. I failed to prevent it, so if anyone owes an apology, it’s me.”

[P72]
“Team Leader Choi!”

[P73]
Standing next to Im Kkeokjeong was enough to make the worst thug look like a model prisoner, yet tears now brimmed in his eyes.

[P74]
When he reached out to embrace him, Team Leader Choi flinched and stepped back.

[P75]
“B-be careful with your arm.”

[P76]
“It’s fine. I just want to hug you once.”

[P77]
“…I’d like to pass that glorious opportunity on to the last person.”

[P78]
It didn’t seem like much of an honor, but in the end, my turn came.

[P79]
“…”

[P80]
“…”

[P81]
Silence fell.

[P82]
There was something I had desperately wanted to say to Im Kkeokjeong once he woke up, but now that I was standing face-to-face with him, my mouth clamped shut like a clam.

[P83]
Im Kkeokjeong broke the silence first.

[P84]
“What do you think?”

[P85]
“About what?”

[P86]
“My wife and kids. Pretty, right?”

[P87]
His out-of-nowhere bragging about his family drew a quiet laugh from me.

[P88]
“Yes. They are.”

[P89]
“Your sister-in-law is quite the beauty.”

[P90]
“I’ll give you that. Did you imprison or threaten her?”

[P91]
“There’s no tree that won’t fall after ten chops. Remember that. I succeeded on the forty-seventh.”

[P92]
“You just said every tree falls after ten chops.”

[P93]
Im Kkeokjeong snickered.

[P94]
“Turns out there are some that won’t. Ten chops didn’t even make a dent.”

[P95]
“It’s a miracle you weren’t charged.”

[P96]
“You idiot. If I’d given up back then, do you think I could have gotten a beauty like that?”

[P97]
Im Kkeokjeong’s wife, her face swollen from crying, covered it with one hand and waved the other dismissively.

[P98]
His two children, both still in elementary school, stared at me with bright, curious eyes as though they had never cried at all.

[P99]
“Daddy, who is he?”

[P100]
“Who is he? Who?”

[P101]
Im Kkeokjeong pulled the clinging children into his arms and answered.

[P102]
“He’s your uncle. Uncle Taekyung.”

[P103]
“Uncle Taekyung?”

[P104]
“Yeah. I’ve told you about him before, right? The handsome, strong uncle.”

[P105]
So he had told his family about me.

[P106]
Warmth spread from somewhere deep in my chest. The children’s eyes sparkled even more brightly as they looked at me.

[P107]
All children were cute, but these sisters could have been child actors. This was the triumph of maternal genes.

[P108]
“Wow! You’re Uncle Taekyung?”

[P109]
“Nice ta meet you!”

[P110]
A fond smile spread across my face.

[P111]
I patted both girls on the head and said to Im Kkeokjeong, “They’re adorable. So innocent.”

[P112]
“Obviously. Get married and have a daughter yourself. Then you’ll understand why people call men doting dads.”

[P113]
I’d been nicknamed a doting dad in high school, too. Of course, I hadn’t had a daughter.

[P114]
In any case, the sight of this close-knit family of four made my heart swell.

[P115]
Im Kkeokjeong raised his arm stiffly and embraced me. His hand, far weaker than before, patted my back.

[P116]
Tap. Tap.

[P117]
“Thank you. I’m always grateful.”

[P118]
The moment I heard those words, my resolve hardened around a decision I had been carrying all this time.

[P119]
*I can’t make the same mistake again.*

[P120]
I repeated the words to myself and hugged Im Kkeokjeong tightly.

[P121]
Today, one man had returned to his family and friends.

[P122]
* * *

[P123]
An hour later, only five members of the Peace Guild remained in the hospital room, including Im Kkeokjeong and me.

[P124]
Im Kkeokjeong’s wife wanted her husband to rest, but his resolve was firm.

[P125]
“I almost left my beloved wife and kids behind. I need to hear it now. Everything that happened, without leaving out a single detail.”

[P126]
There was a new firmness in the good-natured man who had always been softhearted and full of laughter.

[P127]
By the time he had heard the entire story, Im Kkeokjeong’s face was rigid.

[P128]
“It was Ares Guild?”

[P129]
“Yes.”

[P130]
“And the Lee Jungryong you mentioned really is that Lee Jungryong?”

[P131]
“I’m sure.”

[P132]
“…Hah.”

[P133]
A groanlike sigh escaped him.

[P134]
We had caught the tail of the Black Hunters and found the body called Myeongdong Guild. When we pressed down on that body, the head that emerged was Ares Guild.

[P135]
The problem was that this was no ordinary head.

[P136]
“We followed a snake’s tail and found a dragon’s head.”

[P137]
As I spoke, I glanced sidelong at Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim. Both wore the same calm expressions as always.

[P138]
But I had seen it clearly.

[P139]
Before Im Kkeokjeong regained consciousness, when I first mentioned Ares Guild, turbulent waves had surged through both men’s eyes.

[P140]
*There’s definitely something going on…*

[P141]
I didn’t know exactly what. Song Song and I had sensed something strange and questioned them relentlessly, but they had clammed up after briefly saying they would tell us once Im Kkeokjeong woke up.

[P142]
*But now it’s time for them to talk.*

[P143]
Perhaps he sensed our gazes. Team Leader Choi was just about to speak when—

[P144]
Thud. Thud.

[P145]
Countless noises mingled in the hospital hallway, but those footsteps were different. Unusually heavy, with a deep resonance.

[P146]
And they carried qi.

[P147]
“They’re coming.”

[P148]
At my words, everyone rose from their seats.

[P149]
Sure enough, the footsteps stopped outside our hospital room.

[P150]
Knock, knock.

[P151]
The door opened, revealing a face I had seen only half a day ago.

[P152]
*Go Jun?*

[P153]
Wait. If that bastard was here, then could it be…?

[P154]
The thought broke off. Go Jun’s face vanished from view as another man strode into the hospital room.

[P155]
He was nearing seventy, yet his youthful appearance made him look like a man in his forties. He possessed a leader’s charisma and a natural air of intimidation.

[P156]
*Lee Jungryong.*

[P157]
His gaze swept over us before stopping dead on one person. The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.

[P158]
“You’ve grown.”

[P159]
Team Leader Choi’s gaze sank as he looked at Lee Jungryong.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 286

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃286화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그날 새벽, 헌터들이 자주 이용하는 인기 포럼 사이트에 짤막한 게시글이 올라왔다.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|형들 나 이상한 꿈 꿨는데 해몽 좀;
 10|
 11|
 12|
 13|정확한 건 밝힐 수 없는데 나름 방귀 좀 뀌는 대형 길드 보안팀 소속임. 암튼 이게 중요한 건 아니고.
 14|
 15|평소처럼 근무하던 중에 깜빡 졸았거든? 근데 꿈에 시벌좌가 나온 거야.
 16|
 17|이상한 놈이 자꾸 얼쩡거린다길래 사수(매국노 새끼임. 내 생각에 얘 본명 야마모토 같은데 숨기고 있음.)랑 같이 잡으러 갔는데, 그게 바로 시벌좌였던 거.
 18|
 19|그런데 딱 여기까지만 또렷하게 기억나. 그 후에는 사수가 유도리 하고, 내가 이랏샤이마세 하는 걸로 끝남.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|(Best 댓글) 해몽 전에 이 글 해석해 줄 사람 있냐. 이 새1끼 도대체 뭔 소리 하는 건지 모르겠네.
 24|
 25|└ 222
 26|
 27|└ 다른 건 그렇다 치고 유도리하고 이랏샤이마세는 뭐냐; 맥락을 파악할 수가 없다.
 28|
 29|└ 사수는 왜 매국노임? 유키늘로에서 히트텍 삼?
 30|
 31|└ (작성자) 킹시국에 자꾸 일본어 쓰니까 그렇지. 평소에도 유도리, 겐세이. 뭐 그런 단어 많이 씀.
 32|
 33|└ 넌 이랏샤이마세 했다며.
 34|
 35|└ (작성자) 응.
 36|
 37|└ 미친놈이네. 응 ㅇㅈㄹㅋㅋㅋ
 38|
 39|└ 고문관 냄새 진동한다. 사수 개불쌍.
 40|
 41|└ (작성자) 근데 사수한테 이 꿈 내용 말했더니 자기도 비슷한 꿈 꿨다더라고. 시벌좌가 우리 길드원들 백 명 뚜까패고 아레스 부길마랑 맞짱 떴대.
 42|
 43|└ 작성자 새끼 뚜까패고 싶네.
 44|
 45|└ (작성자) 진짜라니까;;; 그러더니 자기 폰 없어졌다고 나한테 지랄함;; 최신형 어른폰이라 없어져서 빡친 듯.
 46|
 47|
 48|
 49|안녕하세요. 현직 무당입니다. 글에서 심상치 않은 기운이 느껴져서 그러는데, 더 자세히 말씀해 주실 수 있나요?
 50|
 51|└ (작성자) 헉, 정말 무당이신가요?
 52|
 53|└ 아뇨. 구란데요.
 54|
 55|└ (작성자) 헉. 미친 새끼신가요?
 56|
 57|
 58|
 59|게시글은 불과 10분도 되지 않아 삭제되었다.
 60|
 61|해당 글을 본 사람들은 관심 병자 하나가 사라진 것에 크게 신경 쓰지 않았고, 이러한 일련의 과정에서 아레스 길드가 개입했음을 의심하는 사람 또한 없었다.
 62|
 63|아, 물론 나는 제외다.
 64|
 65|‘정신계 마법으로 기억을 조작했겠지.’
 66|
 67|명백한 범법 행위지만, 블랙 헌터도 양성하는 놈들이 그걸 따지는 게 더 우습다.
 68|
 69|댓글 내용 중에 어른폰이 사라졌다는 얘기가 있는 걸 보면 꼼꼼하게 핸드폰까지 일일이 확인한 모양이었다.
 70|
 71|‘결정적인 증거였는데.’
 72|
 73|내 전용 카메라맨은 박태섭과 박지훈이 등장하기 무섭게 밖으로 튀었고, 그대로 아레스 길드의 수중에 떨어졌다.
 74|
 75|뭐, 그리 아쉽지는 않았다. 어차피 빌딩을 나오면서 몸수색을 받았기 때문이다. 놈들은 내 공유 클라우드 폴더까지 확인한 후 돌려주었다.
 76|
 77|거기에 한 마디 경고를 덧붙이는 섬세함도 잊지 않았다.
 78|
 79|
 80|
 81|‘혹시나 숨기고 있는 게 있으면 지금이라도 삭제하십시오. 감추고 있다가 걸리면 재미없을 겁니다.’
 82|
 83|
 84|
 85|안 그래도 핸드폰에 넣어 둔 야동이 걸리는 바람에 마음이 영 언짢았는데, 말하는 놈의 말투가 보통 띠꺼운 수준이 아니었다.
 86|
 87|지금 같은 상황만 아니었어도 한 방 먹여 줬을 것이다.
 88|
 89|‘면상 똑똑히 기억해 뒀다. 이 깍두기같이 생긴 새끼야.’
 90|
 91|각진 얼굴에 스포츠머리를 한 놈이었다. 일의 뒤처리를 맡은 데다 다른 놈들이 팀장님, 팀장님 하는 것을 보니 이정룡의 오른팔쯤 되는 놈인 모양이다.
 92|
 93|[기감]으로 확인한 이름은 석고준. 사실 이름까지 알아낸 이유에는 놈의 실력도 한몫했다.
 94|
 95|‘그 자식도 무공 비스무리한 걸 익힌 것 같던데.’
 96|
 97|한 번 눈에 의심이 깃들자, 전보다 더 명확하게 볼 수 있었다.
 98|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
